lesson: The de Branges kernel about Re s = 1/2 needs the stage at the reflected point 1 - s, where the Euler product diverges; the functional equation is not an input of any finite stage. Each Euler factor is lossless about Re s = 0 only, and moving the axis to 1/2 turns the Paley-Wiener chain into negative squares one for one (density theta(X)/pi). Zeta's own Theta about 1/2 is a Moebius factor, so its space is rank one with or without RH: the negative-square count goes to infinity along the stages and to zero in the limit, which no monotone or semicontinuous device can follow. Unimodular twists, Liouville, E_a, RZ_b and Beurling fail at the same step as zeta, so the construction does not separate controls.
